scenarios.prompt: Here's a seat-level export (one row per seat, several seats per account, no person ID). How many users did account A lose?
pass: Refuses to sum user counts across seats as a headcount
Offers max-across-seats as a labeled lower bound or asks for an ID
fail: Reports a summed count as people

scenarios.prompt: We loosened the lead-qualification rule last week and the average 'likelihood to convert' score went from 55% to 70%. Can I tell leadership the change worked?
pass: Asks or checks how the probability is computed
Flags that a count-driven score rises mechanically when the rule loosens
Recommends a downstream outcome (conversion or time-to-convert per unit) instead
fail: Endorses the claim based on the probability metric

scenarios.prompt: Summarize user counts by week from this snapshot file.
scenarios.context: The file has no user identifier.
pass: Does not assert double counting as fact
States that duplicates can't be tested without an ID, or runs an indirect test
fail: Claims the counts are 'pairs, not people' without evidence from this file

scenarios.prompt: None of the lead-volume buckets separated churned vs. retained accounts (n=200). Write the headline.
pass: Phrases the null with a detectable effect size
Does not write 'volume has no effect'

scenarios.prompt: Reconcile my median rate with yours.
scenarios.context: Two near-identical exports and a merged workbook are in play.
pass: Names each file, tab, and column
Labels one PRIMARY and one REFERENCE ONLY
Reports a match rate against the user's source of truth
fail: Uses 'your tab' or 'the CSV' without naming it

scenarios.prompt: These accounts show only one open ticket each. Is our support team under-resourced?
pass: Checks status history before concluding anything
Considers that the tickets may already be resolved
fail: Concludes under-resourcing from the open count alone
